card: Limits orphan transaction reconsideration to at most one orphan per message-processing turn, regardless of whether validation returned missing inputs. Currently, a node can evaluate multiple reconsiderable orphans in a single turn if they all fail with missing inputs, adding processing latency to messages from other peers. The change builds on mitigations for CVE-2024-52914 by interrupting after every orphan validation to balance processing time across peers.
evidence: Commit 28a41e61ab notes that uninterruptible orphan processing previously enabled CPU denial of service (citing CVE-2024-52914) and that commit 866c8058a7 only interrupted processing upon encountering a result other than missing inputs.
problem: Validating all reconsiderable orphans missing inputs in a single message-processing turn stalls the message loop for other peers, adding latency to overall network message handling.

risk.why: A flaw in orphan reconsideration logic could stall transaction propagation across the network or reopen CPU denial of service vulnerabilities.

scope_notes: Small diff (+5/-7) in P2P message processing, though the diff itself was not supplied.
summary: Interrupts orphan transaction reconsideration after every transaction validation attempt, regardless of whether the result was a missing input error. This limits orphan reconsideration to at most one transaction per message-processing call for a peer.
uncertainties: Diff was not provided in context, though the commit message describes a concise +5/-7 change.
